# Next Notes

> Dictation and meeting notes for macOS that run entirely on the user's own Mac. Hold a
> key and speak, and the cleaned-up sentence appears at the cursor in whatever app is
> already focused. Sit in a meeting and the notes write themselves. No account, no
> subscription, no server, and no bot joining the call.

Next Notes is free and open source, and requires macOS 26 on Apple silicon.

## What it does

- **Dictation into any app.** Hold one key, speak, release. The text is transcribed and
  punctuated locally, then inserted where the cursor already was — no window to switch to.
  It learns the names and jargon you use, so it stops mangling them.
- **Meeting notes without a bot.** It reads your calendar and starts when the meeting
  does, after asking. Your microphone and your speaker output are captured as two separate
  tracks, which is how the transcript attributes who said what without anything joining
  the call.
- **Follow-ups it proposes, never sends.** It can draft the follow-up while you talk. It
  offers; you approve. Nothing is created or sent on its own.
- **It writes where the work already is.** Calendar, Gmail, Drive and Docs, in your own
  account, acting as you.

## How the privacy claim actually works

This is the part most comparable tools do differently, so it is worth stating precisely:

- **Transcribed on the device.** Apple's on-device speech recogniser, or NVIDIA Parakeet
  through CoreML. Audio becomes words on the machine it was spoken to.
- **Summarised on the device.** A local language model (Qwen3.5-4B) reads the transcript
  and writes the summary, the decisions, and who owes what. It is downloaded once and then
  runs offline.
- **Stored on the device.** One folder per meeting under Application Support. Recordings
  are deleted once the notes are written, unless you ask to keep them.
- There is no server to send any of it to. There is no account to create.

## Comparable tools

People generally arrive at Next Notes from Wispr Flow (dictation) or Granola (meeting
notes). The difference that matters is where the work happens: both of those upload audio
to be processed. Next Notes does not upload anything, which is also why it is limited to
recent Apple silicon Macs.
